306654.subject: Physics
306654.text: Consider a continuous X-ray photon emitted from a Coolidge tube. The energy of this photon is derived from
options: the kinetic energy of the free electrons in the target
the kinetic energy of the striking electron
an atomic transition within the target
the kinetic energy of the ions in the target
306654.sol: Continuous X-rays are produced due to the deceleration of high-speed electrons when they strike the target material in a Coolidge tube. The loss in the kinetic energy of these striking electrons is emitted as continuous X-ray photons, also known as Bremsstrahlung radiation. Characteristic X-rays, on the other hand, are produced due to atomic transitions within the target atoms. Thus, the energy of a continuous X-ray photon is derived from the kinetic energy of the striking electron.

306591.subject: Physics
306591.text: Suppose n_p and n_e represent the numbers of holes and conduction electrons, respectively, in an intrinsic semiconductor.
306591.sol: In an intrinsic semiconductor, charge carriers are generated by the thermal excitation of electrons from the valence band to the conduction band. Each excitation creates exactly one free electron in the conduction band and leaves behind exactly one hole in the valence band. Therefore, the number of conduction electrons is always equal to the number of holes, which gives n_p = n_e .
